ai.thread_title: Running Agent Code Safely in Isolated Sandboxes
ai.name: Simon Willison & Prime Radiant
ai.hook: Simon Willison published patterns for running agent-generated code in isolated sandboxes.
insights: Three sandbox options published: **WebAssembly**, QEMU (virtual machine), and **Apple Container isolation**
Prevents agents from damaging your Mac even if misdirected or prompt-injected
Demonstrated with Claude Code, Superpowers, and other agent systems; working demos included
ai.for_you: If your agency runs agents for clients or on client machines, this solves a major liability risk. You can safely let agents execute code without worrying about system damage. Worth testing with one client project this week to build confidence.
ai.context: Agent systems are increasingly running code on user machines. The safety question is: what stops a compromised agent from deleting files, stealing data, or breaking the system? Sandboxing is the proven answer.
ai.what_changed: Willison and Prime Radiant published full write-up with working demos showing three different sandbox strategies. This is actionable, not theoretical.
ai.action: test, because isolating agent code execution is critical for client trust and your agency's insurance and liability.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only concrete safety pattern for running agents on client machines published this week; directly applicable to agency delivery.

ai.thread_title: Enterprise Agents Moving from Chatbots to Workflow Orchestrators
ai.name: Aaron Levie
ai.hook: Aaron Levie signals shift from agents answering questions to agents orchestrating complex tasks.
insights: Phase 1 (past): Agents that spit out quick answers for users
Phase 2 (now): **Agents you orchestrate inside a set of tasks**, fan out to sub-tasks, work in parallel
Token spend per employee continues rising; adoption curve remains early
ai.for_you: This means your agency should focus on building agents that AUTOMATE work (not just answer questions). Think: an agent that checks approvals, pulls documents, runs checks, and reports back — not an agent that answers 'what is my budget?'. This is how PT SMBs will get ROI.
ai.context: Enterprise use of agents is maturing from Q&A systems to autonomous workflow executors. This is a mental model shift: agents as workers, not assistants.
ai.what_changed: Levie published new post explicitly naming this shift. Previous thinking treated agents as answer engines; now they're task coordinators.
ai.action: investigate, because your client pitches should shift from 'agent that answers questions' to 'agent that completes workflows.'
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Clear signal about how enterprise AI work is maturing; directly impacts agency positioning.

insights: Agents identified audit risks and decision points that experienced auditors missed
477 points on Hacker News; professional context (not benchmark gaming)
Applies to Portuguese SMB accounting: **agents can augment or replace routine audit work**
ai.for_you: This validates that agents can handle specialized SMB work (accounting, compliance, audit) at expert level. Your clients in accounting, finance, or legal might hire you to build agents that do routine audit or compliance checks. Worth bringing to those conversations.
ai.context: Most AI benchmarks are games. This is a real-world professional services trial. Agents beat experienced humans on a task requiring judgment and domain knowledge.
ai.what_changed: Real-world trial results published; first credible evidence agents outperform accountants on reasoning, not just speed.
ai.action: investigate, because this opens up new agency offerings for PT SMBs in regulated services (accounting, audit, compliance).
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Real-world expert comparison, not benchmark marketing; directly applicable to Portuguese SMB services.
